newsitem.title: USA: Delta places $800 million engine order.
newsitem.headline: Delta places $800 million engine order.

text.p: Delta Air Lines said it has placed an $800 million order with CFM International for CFM56-7 engines to power 70 Boeing Next-Generation 737 aircraft scheduled to begin delivery in mid-1998.
CFM International is a 50/50 joint company between General Electric Co and Snecma of France.
Earlier, Delta announced that it had signed an exclusive $15 billion pact with Boeing covering Delta's aircraft needs for the next 20 to 25 years.
The CFM56-7 is the exclusive powerplant for the Boeing 737-600, 737-700 and 737-800 aircraft.

"Our relationship with Delta Air Lines goes back a long way...The confidence Delta has shown by selecting the CFM56-7-powered 737 as the foundation of its narrow body fleet for the next 20 years is highly gratifying," said CFM International North American sales director Dick Papes.
Delta's order brings the total of announced Next-Generation 737 aircraft orders to 605, making this the fastest-selling engine/aircraft combinatioon in aviation history.
